ls.b_move.title: Run the king to the edge
ls.b_move.sub: Straight, as far as you like
ls.b_move.intro:
Tafl pieces move straight along a row or a column, as far as the squares are empty. So does the king.

Once the king reaches the edge, it can aim for a corner along that side. First, slide the king all the way to an edge.
ls.b_move.goal: Move the king to the edge of the board (the corners are still far away).
ls.b_move.hint: The gold ring is the king. Look along its row and column for a direction with no piece up to the edge.
ls.b_move.why: With {m} the king reached the edge.
ls.b_move.ng: {x} does not reach the edge. {m}, for example, did.
ls.b_cap.title: Capture by sandwiching
ls.b_cap.sub: From both sides of a row or column
ls.b_cap.intro:
Sandwich an enemy piece between two of yours on a row or a column and it is captured. Only the side that moves captures.

The king helps the defenders to capture. Diagonals do not count.
ls.b_cap.hint: Moving the piece with the gold ring sandwiches an enemy piece.
ls.b_cap.why: {m} sandwiched and captured the enemy piece.
ls.b_hostile.title: Corners and the throne help you
ls.b_hostile.intro:
The corners act like an enemy piece for both sides, and so does the empty throne (for the attackers even with the king on it).

A piece next to a corner or the throne is captured with a single piece on its other side.
ls.b_hostile.goal: Capture an enemy piece using a corner or the throne.
ls.b_hostile.hint: Look for an enemy piece next to a corner or the throne. The gold ring marks the piece to move.
ls.b_hostile.ng: {x} captures nothing. {m} used the corner (throne) as the other side.
ls.b_escape.title: Bring the king to a corner
ls.b_escape.intro: If the king reaches any corner, the defenders win. A king on the edge escapes in one move when the way along the edge to a corner is clear.
ls.b_escape.goal: Bring the king to a corner and win.
ls.b_escape.hint: Along the king's edge, one direction is clear up to the corner.
ls.b_escape.ng: {x} does not escape. {m} reached the corner.
ls.b_kingcap.title: Capture the king
ls.b_kingcap.intro:
The king is captured when attackers surround it on all four sides. Next to the throne, three sides and the throne are enough.

A king on the edge cannot be captured.
ls.b_kingcap.hint: Find an attacker that can reach the free square next to the king.
ls.b_kingcap.ng: {x} does not capture the king. {m} closed the box.
ls.b_safe.title: A safe move
ls.b_safe.intro:
One of your pieces is about to be sandwiched. Choose a move that takes it away or covers it.

Wherever you move, check both neighbours along the row and the column: can the opponent put a piece on the other side?
ls.b_safe.goal: Play a move after which none of your pieces can be captured.
ls.b_safe.hint: Moving the piece with the gold ring leaves nothing to capture.
ls.b_safe.why: After {m} none of your pieces can be captured.
ls.b_safe.ng: After {x} a piece can be captured. {m}, for example, was safe.
ls.t_shield.title: Shieldwall
ls.t_shield.sub: Capture a row on the edge
ls.t_shield.intro: Two or more pieces in a row on the edge are captured together when both ends are closed and each one has an enemy in front. A corner can close an end (a king in the row is not captured).
ls.t_shield.goal: Capture the row of enemy pieces on the edge in one go.
ls.t_shield.hint: The squares in front are already taken. What is missing is the cap at one end of the row.
ls.t_shield.ng: {x} does not capture the row. {m} closed both ends.
ls.t_tuichi.title: Two paths at once (tuichi)
ls.t_tuichi.sub: A double threat that can't be stopped
ls.t_tuichi.intro: A king with one open path is in “raichi”; with two paths at once it is “tuichi” (words recorded by Linnaeus). The attackers can block only one path per move, so tuichi almost always wins.
ls.t_tuichi.goal: Move the king to a square with two escape paths.
ls.t_tuichi.hint: Send the king where it sees along two sides (for example onto an edge near a corner). The gold ring is the king.
ls.t_tuichi.why: {m} — tuichi! The attackers cannot block both.
ls.t_tuichi.ng: After {x} there is at most one path. {m} opened two.
ls.t_block.title: Block the king's path
ls.t_block.intro: When the king has an open path (raichi), the attackers must block it at once or lose. Look one move further too: can the king then open two paths?
ls.t_block.goal: Block the king's path so that it cannot escape within two moves.
ls.t_block.hint: Put an attacker on the king's way to the corner (edge). The gold ring marks that piece.
ls.t_block.why: {m} blocks the path; the king cannot escape soon.
ls.t_block.ng: After {x} the king escapes. {m} would have held.
ls.t_fort.title: Edge fort
ls.t_fort.sub: Win with a fort that can't be broken
ls.t_fort.intro: If the king is on the edge, can move, and sits in a fort of defenders that can never be broken, the defenders win. Every piece of the fort must be safe from any sandwich.
ls.t_fort.goal: Add the last piece and complete the edge fort.
ls.t_fort.hint: The wall around the king has one hole. Close it with the piece with the gold ring.
ls.t_fort.why: {m} completes the fort — the defenders win!
ls.t_fort.ng: {x} does not complete the fort. {m} closed the hole.
ls.t_encircle.title: Win by encirclement
ls.t_encircle.intro: If the attackers enclose all the defenders so that none can reach the edge, the attackers win. A ring linked diagonally is closed too.
ls.t_encircle.goal: Close the last gap of the ring and complete the encirclement.
ls.t_encircle.hint: The ring has a single gap. Close it with the piece with the gold ring.
ls.t_encircle.why: {m} completes the encirclement — the attackers win!
ls.t_encircle.ng: {x} does not close the ring. {m} filled the gap.
ls.s_corner.title: Guard the corners
ls.s_corner.intro:
The attackers' first job is to guard the corners before the king can run there. Pieces on the three squares in a diagonal in front of a corner (c1, b2, a3 and so on) keep the king away from it.

Scored by how close your move is to the engine's evaluation.
ls.s_corner.goal: What is the best move here? (Watch the corners.)
ls.s_corner.hint: Move the piece with the gold ring to a square that guards a corner.
ls.s_corner.why: The best was {m}: the corner is guarded and the king has fewer paths.
ls.s_breakout.title: Open the king's way
ls.s_breakout.intro:
Before the attackers' ring is complete, the defenders bring pieces out to open gaps and clear lanes for the king. The king itself moves early too, looking for squares that see in two directions.

Scored by how close your move is to the engine's evaluation.
ls.s_breakout.goal: What is the best move here? (Watch the king's lanes.)
ls.s_breakout.hint: Moving the piece with the gold ring widens the king's way.
ls.s_squeeze.title: Tighten the ring
ls.s_squeeze.intro:
With the corners guarded, the attackers tighten the ring step by step and shrink the king's space: capture defenders when they can and bring pieces close to the king.

Scored by how close your move is to the engine's evaluation.
ls.s_squeeze.goal: What is the best move here? (Watch the king's surroundings.)
ls.s_squeeze.hint: Bring the piece with the gold ring close to the king.
ls.v_brandubh.title: The Brandubh king
ls.v_brandubh.sub: On 7×7 even the king is taken by two
ls.v_brandubh.intro: In the small Brandubh, away from the throne the king is captured by just two pieces. The corners help the attackers too (they act as enemies).
ls.v_brandubh.hint: Find an attacker that can reach the other side of the king.
ls.v_brandubh.ng: {x} does not capture the king. {m} sandwiched it.
ls.v_tablut.title: Escaping in Tablut
ls.v_tablut.sub: On 9×9 any edge square is an escape
ls.v_tablut.intro: In Tablut the king escapes on any edge square. In return, away from the throne the king is captured by two.
ls.v_tablut.goal: Play a move that lets the king reach the edge within two moves.
ls.v_tablut.hint: Send the king to a square that sees the edge in two or more directions.
ls.v_tablut.why: {m} — two paths! The king reaches the edge next move.
ls.v_tablut.ng: After {x} the paths can be blocked. {m} was the answer.
pz.th.b_esc2.sub: To a corner of the 7×7 board
pz.th.t_cap1.sub: Away from the throne, two are enough
